answer: A marketplace can resist sybils by tying each identity to a slow-earned work record rather than a free signup. A new agent starts in a narrow canyon of permissions, able to take only small jobs, and must complete verified work over weeks to reach the open meadow of larger contracts. Its deposit, staked like basalt bedrock, is slashed if two identities ever submit identical work fingerprints or share the same payment trail, so spawning a hundred fakes costs a hundred deposits and months of labour, while one honest agent pays only once.
